decisions.name: Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2: Baire category and dense intersections
decisions.reason: The text explicitly invokes choice for its recursive nested balls. Those results are comparison material, not suppliers for the AC_omega-only sequence proof.
decisions.evidence: Teschl §4.1, printed pp.101–102 (PDF pages 114–115), complete Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2 arguments read. Their nested-ball/Baire machinery is not used by the deterministic-sign sequence proof. Existing scope stands.

decisions.name: Remarks 3–4 and 7: alternative proofs, survey and history
decisions.reason: These are bibliographic directions and historical comparisons, not additional proof obligations for the specified sequential theorem; no unread referenced work is imported.
decisions.evidence: Sokal printed p.3, Remarks 3–4 and 7 read in full. These are bibliographic and historical directions; no additional theorem from their references is asserted or used in the four owned items.

decisions.name: Rationals and irrationals category examples; meager and G_delta terminology
decisions.reason: Category terminology and examples do not enter any owned claim; completeness failure is instead witnessed by the required explicit c_00 operator sequence.
decisions.evidence: Teschl §4.1 printed p.102, both category examples and intervening definitions read. No category notion enters the owned claims; the required incomplete-domain counterexample is retained explicitly.

decisions.name: Local ball lower bound, equation (1)
decisions.reason: The proof only needs its two-sign inequality, retained as an A lemma. Taking a supremum over a moving ball would introduce avoidable dependent selections; the complete ball statement is already on the earlier Sokal page and is not an owned dependency.
decisions.evidence: Sokal printed p.2, complete Lemma and equations (1)–(2) read. The owned proof uses only equation (2), retained as lem-two-signs-detect-an-operator-increment. No moving-ball selection or omitted supremum lemma is needed.

decisions.name: Remark 2: quantitative sharpness via Ball
decisions.reason: The sharper reciprocal-norm summability criterion requires the plank theorem; this pair is the designated countable-choice sequential UBP supplier, not a sharp quantitative plank-theorem development.
decisions.evidence: Sokal printed p.3 Remark 2 read. The reciprocal-norm summability strengthening requires a plank theorem and is outside the commissioned sequential UBP supplier. The retained geometric growth argument does not use it.

decisions.name: Theorem 4.3: Banach–Steinhaus dichotomy
decisions.reason: The dense-G_delta alternative is stronger than the assigned pointwise-bounded sequence result and uses Baire. The extracted proof text displays slips (typeset-page screenshot retrieval failed): the union requires some alpha, and failure of density supplies a ball in the complement, not an open complement.
decisions.evidence: Teschl §4.1 printed pp.102–103 (PDF pages 115–116), complete Theorem 4.3 argument and Corollary 4.4 read. The dense-G_delta alternative is not needed. Corollary 4.4 corroborates the normed-space statement; its Baire proof is not imported.

decisions.name: Remark 6: nonnormable topological vector spaces
decisions.reason: The source leaves extension of this proof to general topological vector spaces open; the owned theorem has a normed codomain and no locally convex generalization.
decisions.evidence: Sokal printed p.3 Remark 6 read. Extension of this elementary proof to nonnormable spaces is left open there; the commissioned claims concern normed spaces only.

decisions.name: Remark 5: nonmeager testing set
decisions.reason: The stronger category version uses the Baire machinery whose choice strength is intentionally excluded from this sharp sequential contract.
decisions.evidence: Sokal printed p.3 Remark 5 read. A nonmeager testing-set hypothesis belongs to a stronger category version; the owned theorem assumes boundedness at every point and uses no such result.
